summary: One governed command touches the authoritative repository. Everything before it happens in a scratch rehearsal copy and produces the fresh independent-review receipt that the governed command demands.
why_a_rehearsal_is_needed: The fresh review receipt must bind evaluation_receipt_hash == sha256 of the receipt the repair will write, and amphora-phase0-reviewer only signs a receipt it has verified on disk. The replacement receipt is a deterministic function of the worktree (bundle bytes, parent hashes, claim locks, the two locked-benchmark replays, and a deterministic Ed25519 signature), so it can be produced in a copy first. `re-evaluate --dry-run` publishes that exact hash in advance, and the governed command refuses if the supplied review binds anything else - so a mismatch can only ever produce a refusal, never a bad write.

step_0_read_the_plan.command: target/debug/amphora-tui portfolio phase0 re-evaluate --module <MODULE> --reason "<why this binding is broken>" --as-of <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ> --evaluation-key /home/ubuntu/.local/share/amphora/phase0/keys/evaluator.ed25519.seed --review <any existing signed review for <MODULE>> --dry-run
step_0_read_the_plan.writes: nothing (the dry run is wrapped in prove_read_only)

step_1_rehearse_in_a_scratch_copy.note: amphora-cli resolves its workspace root at compile time (env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")), so the rehearsal needs its own build; a binary built from the authoritative tree would write to the authoritative tree.
step_1_rehearse_in_a_scratch_copy.if_the_hash_differs: STOP. Do not proceed. A difference means the replacement receipt is not a deterministic function of the tree, and the governed command would refuse anyway.

step_2_obtain_the_fresh_independent_revi.where: the scratch copy; the reviewer writes its receipt outside any repository
step_2_obtain_the_fresh_independent_revi.produces: a review receipt whose evaluation_receipt_hash == <S>, signed by the second, distinct trusted identity

step_3_the_one_governed_command.command: flock -w 300 .cron.lock target/debug/amphora-tui portfolio phase0 re-evaluate --module <MODULE> --reason "<why this binding is broken>" --as-of <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ> --evaluation-key /home/ubuntu/.local/share/amphora/phase0/keys/evaluator.ed25519.seed --review /home/ubuntu/wv1-reviews/<MODULE>.review.v1.dsse.json
what_it_does_in_one_transaction: refuses unless <MODULE> is in UNBOUND_BENCHMARK_RESULTS and its shipped result is in fact unbound from its signed receipt
refuses unless BOTH a fresh external evaluator key AND a fresh, distinct, trusted, signed independent-review receipt are supplied
refuses unless the supplied review binds the exact receipt this run will write

archives the prior evaluation receipt, independent-review receipt, benchmark result, movement event and movement ledger under <MODULE>/evidence/phase0/superseded/<sha256-of-prior-evaluation-receipt>/ with a supersession note
regenerates benchmark/result.v1.json through evaluate_signed(), the single legitimate writer, and writes the replacement evaluation receipt
re-binds the review through the existing import_review() path
restores the module byte-for-byte from a backup if any step fails
step_3_the_one_governed_command.leaves_the_module_at: PRE_PHASE_0, promotable - the prior movement event bound the prior receipt hash and was superseded with it

step_4_re_derive_the_phase.note: phase is derived from a fresh movement event with two distinct trusted signatures; it is never asserted by the repair.

step_5_reconcile_the_guard.note: UNBOUND_BENCHMARK_RESULTS in amphora-cli/src/phase0.rs and the pinned counts in tests::source_ledger_historical_movement_and_status_are_read_only must be updated in the same change that repairs a module, or the regression guard shipped_benchmark_results_stay_bound_to_signed_evaluation_receipts will fail - by design.
